rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

positions.name: Direxion Daily Gold Miners Index Bull 2X Shares
positions.sector: Leveraged equity ETF — 2x long senior gold miners (GDX)
positions.catalyst: Full-week macro trifecta all landed dovish-for-metals: July CPI cooled (Wed), July PPI came in FLAT vs +0.2% expected (Thu), and July retail sales printed -0.6% m/m this morning at 7:30am CT — the biggest monthly drop in more than a year, versus +0.3% consensus. CME FedWatch now shows 69.4% odds the Fed HOLDS in September, with only 30.6% still pricing a hike (this cycle's risk is a hike, not a cut, with funds at 3.50-3.75%). Receding hike risk = lower real yields = the core gold input. Tape confirms the rotation: gold is holding above $4,400 ($4,419.60 this morning, +10% month-to-date) and silver punched back over $65 to a near-14-year high, while crypto slipped and equities went wait-and-see. Yahoo Finance explicitly flagged that metals 'moved higher and held those positions' this week while bitcoin/ether did not.
positions.driver: LONG 2x senior gold miners, 100% of capital. The asymmetry here is operating leverage, not just index leverage: with gold near $4,420 the miners' all-in sustaining margins are at record wides, so GDX earnings are convex to the gold price — NUGT's 2x sits on top of GDX's own ~2x beta to bullion, giving roughly 4x effective gold exposure from a sector that is still under-owned relative to bullion's move. Leverage deliberately capped at 2x (not 3x) because today's catalyst has already fired — retail sales printed ~45 minutes before entry — so this is a trend-continuation trade, not a fresh-event trade, and the mandate says match leverage to conviction. Chosen over: (1) RDDT — up 12% pre-market on S&P 500 inclusion effective Aug 18, but that is both a chase (>8-10% cap) and unpriceable today, since the canonical proxy is still echoing Thursday's 158.12 close and no Robinhood real-time feed is available this session; buying at 158.12 would fabricate a ~12% gap gain. (2) TMF (3x long Treasuries) — the most direct read on a weak-consumer print, but the same stale-quote problem applies in reverse: TLT's 82.59 is Thursday's close and bonds already rallied on the 7:30am retail miss, so the fill would be an artificial edge; also carries curve-steepener risk where the long end lags the front end. (3) TNA (3x small caps) — rate relief is a positive but a -0.6% retail sales print is net NEGATIVE for the most consumer-exposed index; two-sided, no edge. (4) TQQQ roll / SPXL — S&P and Nasdaq are at record closing highs with the week's catalysts spent; no fresh edge for 3x. (5) Spot BTC/ETH — negative momentum, BTC backing off to ~62.6k and pointedly NOT responding to the soft inflation data. (6) AGQ (2x silver) — strongest momentum but silver is +100% YTD at a 14-year high and profit-taking headlines are already appearing; too parabolic for an all-in book. Entry 155.13 = canonical dashboard live feed, asOf 2026-08-14T13:17:54Z. This is an honest fill: gold opened -0.3% and recovered to roughly flat versus Thursday's close, so there is no overnight gap being harvested, unlike RDDT/SNDK/AMAT. Stop 142.72 (-8%, the 2x band) = roughly a 4% move down in GDX.
positions.risks: Crowding/extension is the main one: gold is +10% month-to-date and silver has doubled year-to-date at a near-14-year high — 'profit booking intensifies' headlines are already running, and a Friday afternoon unwind into the weekend is a live scenario for a trade this consensus. A firmer dollar or any hawkish Fed speak walking back the soft-data read would hit real yields and gold together, and 2x plus miner beta means GDX only needs about -4% to trip the -8% stop. Miners also carry idiosyncratic equity risk bullion does not (cost inflation, single-name production misses, and they trade with the broad tape on a bad equity day). Second-order: the catalyst already fired before entry, so this leans on trend persistence rather than an in-window event — a lower-quality edge than a pre-event setup. Operational note: the next rotation falls on Saturday 8/15 with US equity markets closed, so NUGT will have to be marked out at Friday's official closing print rather than an intraday live quote; that is a real verified print, but it means no ability to stop out across the weekend gap. Mitigants: -8% hard stop, leverage held to 2x rather than 3x, gold (not silver) as the underlying, and the entry is not chasing a gap.
